newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland seeks better terms of Ruch sale to Hachette.
newsitem.headline: Poland seeks better terms of Ruch sale to Hachette.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry, which has provisionally agreed to sell the news-stand chain Ruch SA to French Hachette Distribution Services, is seeking better terms for the deal, a deputy minister said on Friday.
"We have not finished talks with the investor... I would like to improve...conditions of the sale," Leszek Juchniewicz told a news conference.
"But I would like to complete the privatisation as soon as possible," he added.
In December, the ministry said it had accepted an offer for Ruch from a consortium of Polish firms led Hachette.
But Juchniewicz said the agreement embraced only outline terms and details still needed to hammered out.
He made clear he expected Hachette to make a better offer and to increase Ruch's capital sooner than had been expected. "We would like Ruch's situation to improve right after the sale," he said.
He strongly criticised Hachette for unveiling in French and Polish newspapers its bid for Ruch before a final agreement was reached.

Nowa Europa daily quoted Hachette's president Jean-Louis Nachury as saying his company would pay $84 million for a 75 percent stake in Ruch and then earmark a further $45 million to increase its capital.
Late last month Polish trading company Universal said it was prepared to present an offer for Ruch which it believed was more favourable than Hachette's.
But Juchniewicz ruled out anly talks with Universal as long as the ministry was negotiating the sale with Hachette.
Ruch has a 65 percent share of Poland's press distribution market and owns 17,000 news-stands nationwide. Its net profit in 1995 was 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys.
